current_flow: selection-ui adds the authenticated MIS Reports page at app/(app)/mis-reports: four native selects populated from GET api/mis/options (loaded months plus the server-derived FY 26-27 YTD), Generate posting only the four selectors to POST api/mis/run, and the response branched on its DISCRIMINATED UNION so an unresolvable selection shows zeros plus the 'no mapping configured' notice while a resolved selection with no transactions shows a configured zero result without it. It renders the scope readout, the governed result rows and totals, and the unmapped-GL bucket as a reviewable list carrying BOTH Actual and Budget amounts per row. It also makes three small backend changes the grill proved necessary: seeding the admin's DUB plant scope (without which the page cannot work at all), extending MisSelectionBucketRow with those amounts, and populating them in the service. The previously-disabled MIS Reports nav item and the page title are enabled. Design skills emil-design-eng and frontend-design are mandatory in skills_used, and a functional check covers the resolved path end-to-end.
new_abstractions: the authenticated MIS Reports page branching on the resolved/unresolvable response union rather than row emptiness
the unmapped-GL bucket as a reviewable list carrying both Actual and Budget amounts per row
the first data methods on the existing cookie/CSRF api client

criteria_map.an authenticated MIS Reports page presen: KEEP (amended). The page renders the four native selects from the options route and Generate posts only the four selectors — but the seeded admin had NO DUB plant scope, so the happy path was unusable; this task now seeds it. A fourth required test also proves the returned result rows and totals are actually RENDERED, so the page cannot pass its leaves while showing nothing.
criteria_map.the page shows a resolved-scope readout: KEEP. The scope readout plus the two zero states, branched on the response UNION rather than row emptiness. The unresolvable branch is proven by the component test against a mocked response, because the single-selection master makes it unreachable from the live UI.
criteria_map.the unmapped-GL bucket is rendered as a: KEEP (amended). The bucket renders as a reviewable list, but MisSelectionBucketRow carried NO amount, so this task extends the contract and the service: each row shows BOTH its Actual and its Budget amount for the period, with costCentre null for Budget-only rows. Decision 0018 was amended to record that mis-selection renders the LIST while mis-statement renders the bucket LINE.

gaps: P0 - the authenticated happy path was unusable: the seeded admin has the report permission but NO DUB user_scope, so plantScope(user) is empty, the options route returns nothing and a DUB run is rejected. The plan assumed task 2 delivered a usable actor; it did not.

P0 - C3 was impossible with a frontend-only change: MisSelectionBucketRow carries no amount and the service returns only its metadata, and generic GL/month result rows cannot safely reconstruct an amount per composite key.

P0 - bucket ownership contradicted an active decision: 0018 assigns visible bucket rendering to mis-statement while this task requires it, and the later human delivery-boundary answer supporting a selector bucket list was never reconciled into the decision.

P0 - the functional check's no-mapping case was unreachable: the master has exactly one selection (Agriculture/Nursery/DUB) and the options endpoint derives its controls from master selections, so the UI cannot offer a non-matching combination; the stated live walkthrough could not be performed.

P1 - 'governed numbers' had no specified UI surface or proof: C1's required test proved only selector population and the POST payload, so the page could satisfy its leaves without ever rendering result rows or totals.

P1 - bucket semantics were undefined: Budget-only bucket entries carry costCentre null so they are not triples, and the plan never decided whether a displayed amount is Actual, Budget, both, or a YTD aggregate.

P1 - verification was incomplete: the task adds a Next.js route but did not require npm run build:frontend, and the new data-client methods had no direct CSRF/credential/one-shot-refresh coverage (api.test.ts covers auth only).
P2 - the grounding overstated nav-drawer.test.tsx: it tests the drawer's toggle, Escape and focus behaviour rather than the nav table, so including it in write_scope was wrong.
resolutions: Seed the admin role's DUB plant scope in backend/src/db/migrate.ts and assert it in migrate.test.ts. Both files are now in write_scope - this task is NOT frontend-only.
Extend MisSelectionBucketRow in contract/src/api.ts and populate it in mis-selection.service.ts; both are now in write_scope, with the controller test proving the amounts.

Decision 0018 has been AMENDED in place with a dated supersession note recording the settled split: mis-selection renders the reviewable LIST (the artifact shown to Srihari), mis-statement renders the bucket LINE inside the statement. Both are required; they are different surfaces, not duplicates.

The FUNCTIONAL CHECK now covers the RESOLVED path end-to-end (slice + scope readout + bucket list), and the UNRESOLVABLE branch is proven by the component test against a mocked unresolvable response. The plan explicitly does not claim a live no-mapping walkthrough that cannot be performed.
Added a FOURTH required test asserting that a resolved response's result rows and totals actually appear on the page, so it cannot pass while showing nothing.

HUMAN-decided (round): each bucket row carries BOTH its Actual and its Budget amount for the selected period, with costCentre NULL for Budget-only rows (GL-only, not triples), so the gap is legible on each side and reconcilable against the slice totals.

verify_commands now include npm run build:frontend, and frontend/src/lib/api.test.ts is in write_scope to cover the new data methods' shared CSRF bootstrap, cookie credentials and one-shot 401 refresh.
nav-drawer.test.tsx is REMOVED from write_scope and listed as unchanged by design; only app-shell.test.tsx moves with the nav table.
open_items: The hierarchical statement, its bucket LINE, and the Excel export belong to mis-statement; drill-down is its own story.
The live no-mapping walkthrough stays unreachable until the master carries more than one selection; the component test covers that branch.
Reconciling the provisional master against Srihari's authoritative Master Table remains the spec's open item - this page is the artifact that drives it.

rounds.question: selection-ui grill (P0/P1): C3 requires the unmapped-GL bucket rendered 'with amounts', but MisSelectionBucketRow currently carries no amount at all — so the contract and service must be extended (this task is not frontend-only). That forces a product decision: the bucket now spans BOTH sides — Actual triples absent from the master (cost centre + GL) and Budget GLs absent from the master (GL only, cost centre null). What should each bucket row show?
options: Both Actual and Budget per row (Rec.)

summary: One cold read returned eight gaps - four blocking - and showed the task was mis-scoped as frontend-only. Seven are repository/decision-answerable and resolved in the amended contract + plan: the seeded admin gains the DUB plant scope without which the page cannot work at all; MisSelectionBucketRow and the service are extended so C3 is achievable; decision 0018 is amended so mis-selection renders the reviewable LIST while mis-statement renders the bucket LINE; the functional check is re-scoped to the resolved path with the unresolvable branch proven by the component test, since a single-selection master makes it unreachable live; a fourth required test proves the governed numbers are actually rendered; build:frontend and api-client CSRF/refresh coverage are added; and nav-drawer.test.tsx is dropped from scope because it tests drawer behaviour, not the nav table. One was a genuine product decision put to the human: each bucket row carries BOTH its Actual and its Budget amount, with costCentre null for Budget-only rows, so the gap is legible on each side. Verdict pass.
